en: Large language models are called large
language models because they have large
neural networks with lots of layers and
parameters in there.
A specific version of large language models
are mixture of experts models,
which means that they are still large, they
still have all these layers and parameters,
but for a given input, they only activate a
subset of these parameters.
So that means that the data does not have to
travel through all these parameters to
produce an output, but only through a
subset, which makes inference, which means
the prediction part, quicker.
It does not mean that you could run such a
model on less powerful hardware because
still all parameters must be loaded into
memory, for example, and that's That's one
of the most tricky parts. That's what
requires a lot of memory.
But when the model then is activated, only a
subset is needed, which makes it quicker.
That is why this architecture is often used
for modern large language models.
